sql: SELECT SUM(trips) AS trips_2025 FROM trips_daily WHERE year(service_date) = 2025
notes: Assumes "completed trips" means all provider types and boroughs in trips_daily for calendar year 2025, summed from the daily grain.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(ontime_pickups) / SUM(total_pickups), 1) AS pickup_otp_pct FROM pickup_otp_daily WHERE standard = '20-minutes' AND year(service_date) = 2025
notes: Assumes the default 20-minute standard (official MTA standard), Primary and Broker pickups only as stored, and 2025 as the full calendar year.

sql:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT SUM(complaints) AS complaints
  FROM complaints_daily WHERE year(opened_date) = 2024
),
t AS (
  SELECT SUM(trips) AS trips
  FROM trips_daily WHERE year(service_date) = 2024
)
SELECT ROUND(1000.0 * c.complaints / t.trips, 2) AS complaint_rate_per_1000
FROM c CROSS JOIN t
notes: Assumes the full calendar year 2024 for both complaints (by opened_date) and completed trips (by service_date), aggregated separately before dividing, with all provider types and categories included.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(no_shows_per_1000), 2) AS provider_no_show_rate FROM provider_no_shows_monthly WHERE provider_type = 'Primary' AND year(month) = 2023
notes: Assumes the no-show rate is the average of monthly no_shows_per_1000 values for Primary across the 12 months of 2023 (the data covers through Dec 2023), reported per 1,000 scheduled trips.

sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(ride_time_min) * 1.0 / SUM(trips), 2) AS avg_ride_time_min FROM ride_time_monthly WHERE year(month) = 2025
notes: Ride time data ends Dec 2023, so the 2025 query will return NULL/empty; assuming the question is answerable only as a no-data result, and the SQL is written per the metric definition in case the data is later extended.
